sections.hypothesis: A short in a delisted coin's Binance USDT-M perpetual, opened at day 1's open after the spot delisting announcement and closed at the removal day's open, earned more than its fees, spread and funding, at 2x leverage with liquidations counted. Hypothetical: Kestrel can't short (P5 parked); the answer decides how much priority derivatives deserve, nothing else.
sections.rationale: Who pays: the same forced and discouraged holders as the spot study (findings item 11): after the announcement, holders who must leave Binance sell into thinning liquidity, and the announcement itself is bad news. Disclosure, and the reason this note exists: the spot fall is already known (-39.8% on average from day 1 to removal, 21 announcements), so this is not an independent test of the fall. It tests what a short would actually have met: whether a perp still traded through the window (Binance closes some before or with the spot delisting; the archive suggests 33 of 36 coins that ever had one were still listed, unverified), whether the perp had already priced the fall (its discount to spot at entry), funding (crowded shorts pay longs), and squeezes (thin coins can spike and liquidate a short). Outside evidence: perps' funding mechanics (Binance's published rules) and the spot study; nothing published on Binance delisting shorts that this note relies on. Not tradable for Luke: Binance futures aren't offered to Australian retail, ASIC caps retail crypto CFD leverage at 2:1, and any provider through his employer needs its personal-trading policy checked; public announcements only. The 13 announcements in the holdout year stay untouched: they are the clean test if derivatives ever open up.
sections.rules: Events: the coins measured in what-happens-between-a-binance-delisting v1 (removed before 2025-11-01, a USDT spot market), whose USDT-M perp (XUSDT, or 1000XUSDT, prices divided by 1,000) traded on day 1 and on the exit day: a daily perp bar with quote volume above zero on both. A perp bar missing on the removal day: exit at the last perp close before it, flagged. Day 0, day 1 and day R as in the spot study. Per coin, on notional: short return = (entry - exit) / entry, entry at the perp's day-1 open, exit at its day-R open; plus funding, summed over every funding settlement after entry and up to exit (a positive rate pays the short, a negative one charges it), from Binance's archive. Leverage 2x (ASIC's retail cap): if any perp daily high from day 1 to day R-1 reaches 1.45 x entry (liquidation at +50% less maintenance margin, rounded), the trade is liquidated: -45% of notional, funding and fees still paid. Also reported at 1x (liquidation at 1.95 x entry). Coins announced together are averaged into one event; the bootstrap runs over announcements. Also reported, deciding nothing: the perp's discount to spot at day 1's open, total funding, the number liquidated, and the worst intra-window rise.
sections.falsification: C is each coin's round trip (costs below). PROCEED (derivatives get higher priority) only if at least 10 announcements have a tradable perp, and the mean over announcements of (2x-leverage short return + funding - 2C) is above 0 with a bootstrap P(> 0) of at least 90%. INSUFFICIENT if fewer than 10 announcements have a tradable perp. Otherwise KILL: shorting delistings is no reason to hurry into derivatives. Run once.
sections.parameters: Fixed before any perp price was looked at: day 1 open entry, day R open exit, 2x leverage with liquidation at 1.45 x entry (1x at 1.95 x reported), funding from the archive, equal weight within an announcement, 5,000 resamples, seed 0. No other entry, leverage or filter is tried; a change is a new version with a reason. No holdout data.
sections.costs: Per coin, one round trip: Binance's base USDT-M taker fee of 5 bps a side (an assumption to check; not in kestrel.toml, which is spot) and the coin's spot half-spread band at day 0's close as the perp's (no perp order-book history), about 0.40% round trip; the test charges 2x that. Funding counted separately as above. Borrow costs don't apply to a perp. Impact at 330 USDT ignored. A study, not a strategy run: one look, logged in the findings.
